articleBody:
Upgrading your garage with built-in workbenches, heavy-duty wall storage, and dedicated tool circuits goes much faster when you complete a few practical preparations upfront.

What to Prepare Before You Start
- [ ] Measure total vehicle parking footprints — Ensuring your cars still fit comfortably protects walkway clearances before ordering deep wall cabinets.
- [ ] Inspect slab edges for dampness or salt efflorescence — Trapping active moisture behind newly framed cabinets or wall finishes causes mildew and wood deterioration.
- [ ] List all high-draw power tools and heaters — Tallying workshop amperage needs tells your contractor whether new dedicated circuits or a subpanel are required.
- [ ] Clear a 36-inch clearance perimeter around the electrical panel — Local building codes prohibit blocking service equipment with permanent shelving or storage.
- [ ] Identify the location of your water heater and furnace — Mechanical appliances require specific clearances from workbenches and combustible storage.
- [ ] Determine desired wall storage mounting heights — Checking stud spacing ensures heavy wall tracks and tool cabinets anchor directly into solid framing.
- [ ] Check garage door sensor and track clearances — Overhead storage racks must clear the open overhead door and torsion spring hardware safely.
- [ ] Decide on heating and insulation goals — Insulating the exterior wall envelope before installing finished drywall keeps heating costs manageable during Colorado winters.

How to Use This Checklist
Walk through your garage with this list in hand and take concrete notes before purchasing materials or requesting quotes. Bringing clear utility and spatial notes to your consultation helps your contractor build an accurate estimate without surprises.
